title: 2027 Reasonable Assurance Plan Update
text:
Tampa Bay Nutrient Management Strategy
This book is the web companion to the 2027 Reasonable Assurance Plan (RA) Update prepared by the Tampa Bay Estuary Program (TBEP) and the Tampa Bay Nitrogen Management Consortium (NMC) for the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) and US Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA). It presents the narrative, figures, and tables of the RA Update for the 2022–2026 reporting period, with each figure and table linked back to the analysis code that produces it in this repository, tbep-tech/reasonable-assurance-analysis.






NoteReproducibility



Figures and tables are generated programmatically, not hand-edited. Run R/dat_proc.R (data assembly) → R/figs.R (figures) and R/docs.R (tables). Loading inputs come from the companion tbep-tech/load-estimates pipeline; water-quality thresholds and segment averaging use the tbeptools R package. All historic and contemporary loading information is openly accessible at https://tbep.org/tampa-bay-nitrogen-loads.


Prior Reasonable Assurance Updates were submitted in 2002, 2007 (with a 2009 Addendum), 2012, 2017, and 2022. As of the 2022 RA Update, FDEP concluded the document “satisfies the requirements for continued approval of the RAP,” and concurred that the proposed NMC corrective actions were “reasonable and sufficient to address the issues in Old Tampa Bay,” requesting periodic updates on corrective-action implementation over the 2022–2026 period.

Headline finding for 2022–2026: FDEP-adopted chlorophyll-a thresholds were met in all major bay segments over the 2022–2026 RA period (see Overview, Figure 2). This represents a marked improvement in overall water quality, particularly in Old Tampa Bay (OTB), which did not meet its chlorophyll-a numeric nutrient criteria in four of the five years of the preceding (2017–2021) period.

Use the sidebar to navigate: the Overview chapter covers the waterbody, water-quality goals, nitrogen loading, and seagrass habitat; the Summary chapter covers corrective actions, progress since 2022, and the delivery-ratio table; and Provenance maps every deliverable to its source code.

title: Overview
text:
1. Description of the Waterbody
The Tampa Bay estuary is located on the eastern shore of the Gulf of Mexico in Florida (Figure 1). At 882 km², it is Florida’s largest open-water estuary. More than 3 million people live in the 5,870 km² watershed. Land use in the watershed is mixed — about 32% undeveloped, 17% agricultural, 42% urban and suburban residential, and the remaining 9% mining. Major habitats include mangroves, salt marshes, salt barrens, and submerged aquatic vegetation.
Between 1950 and 1988, an estimated 42% of the seagrass acreage in Tampa Bay was lost, primarily through excess nitrogen loading and related increases in phytoplankton concentrations that limited light for seagrass survival and growth. In 1980, all municipal wastewater treatment plants were required to provide 100% reuse or Advanced Wastewater Treatment (AWT) for discharges directly to the bay and its tributaries; together with stormwater regulations enacted in the 1980s, these reduced nitrogen loads to the bay. The 1976 TN loadings are more than three times greater than current estimates (1976 = 9,904 tons TN/yr vs. a 2020s annual average of 3,321 tons TN/yr).
The Tampa Bay Nitrogen Management Consortium (NMC) was formed in 1996 and includes local governments and agencies, phosphate companies, port industries, electric utilities, and agricultural interests that work cooperatively in a voluntary framework to maintain nitrogen loads supporting seagrass restoration. In 2020, the TBEP and partners updated the Habitat Master Plan, adopting a goal of maintaining at least 40,000 acres of seagrass baywide.
Between 2022 and 2026, seagrass coverage increased by 1,426 acres baywide, while the Old Tampa Bay segment continued to see losses. Baywide seagrass coverage was estimated at 31,563 acres in 2026, remaining below the 40,000-acre protection and recovery goal for a second consecutive RA assessment period.

title: Overview
section: 1.a. Name:
text:
1.a. Name:
2027 RA Update: No change. This document addresses the four main bay segments of Tampa Bay: Old Tampa Bay, Hillsborough Bay, Middle Tampa Bay and Lower Tampa Bay. As of the 2009 RA Addendum, an additional segment was included: “Remainder of Lower Tampa Bay,” which includes Terra Ceia Bay and portions of the Manatee River and southern Boca Ciega Bay (Figure 5). The Old Tampa Bay, Hillsborough Bay, Middle Tampa Bay and Lower Tampa Bay segments are identical to FDEP’s established estuary nutrient regions; the Remainder of Lower Tampa Bay RA Segment includes FDEP’s Boca Ciega Bay South, Terra Ceia Bay, and Manatee River Estuary nutrient regions (62-302.532(1), F.A.C.).

1.e. Water use classification:
2027 RA Update: Class II and III waters. See rule 62-302.400, F.A.C.

title: Overview
section: 1.f. Designated use of waterbody:
text:
1.f. Designated use of waterbody:
2027 RA Update: No change. Per FDEP’s 2026 303(d)/305(b) Integrated Water Quality Assessment and the 2022–2024 Biennial Assessment, WBIDs in Tampa Bay proper are Category 2 (attaining some designated uses) or 5 (standards not attained, TMDL required). The Category 5 WBIDs in the Old Tampa Bay and Remainder of Lower Tampa Bay segments fall under the RA determination and are therefore treated as Category 4b (a pollutant-control mechanism provides reasonable assurance of future attainment) (Figure 6). This document does not address impairments related to Class II shellfish harvesting areas in Tampa Bay.



Figure 6. FDEP surface-water quality assessment categories for WBIDs intersecting the Tampa Bay watershed.



Figure 6 source: R/figs.R → section wbid attainments · Data: FDEP Nutrients_305b layer × RA segment watershed

title: Overview
section: 1.g. Area of the waterbody:
text:
1.g. Area of the waterbody:
2027 RA Update: No change. The total surface area of the four major bay segments in Tampa Bay is 882 km² (approximately 341 square miles). When including the Remainder of Lower Tampa Bay, the total surface area is 1,006 km² (approximately 389 square miles).

title: Overview
section: 1.h. Pollutant(s) of concern:
text:
1.h. Pollutant(s) of concern:
2027 RA Update: No change. The pollutant of concern is Total Nitrogen (TN), the limiting nutrient in Tampa Bay. Elevated nitrogen loading leads to excess algal growth (indicated by chlorophyll-a concentrations), which reduces light penetration and causes loss of seagrass.

title: Overview
section: 1.i. Suspected or documented sources of pollutant of concern:
text:
1.i. Suspected or documented sources of pollutant of concern:
2027 RA Update: The TBEP has developed loading reports for Tampa Bay since 1985; the most recent estimates cover 2022–2026, openly accessible at https://tbep.org/tampa-bay-nitrogen-loads. Total loadings are less variable than during the 1985–early-2000s period (Figure 7); 2024 loadings were significantly influenced by rainfall from three tropical-storm systems. Per-capita TN loading has decreased over time (Figure 8), as has the amount of TN delivered per unit water in each major bay segment (Figure 9). Hydrologically-normalized total loads remain significantly below 1980s estimates despite a growing metropolitan population (Figure 10).

title: Overview
section: 2.a. Water quality-based targets or aquatic ecological goals:
text:
2.a. Water quality-based targets or aquatic ecological goals:
2027 RA Update: No change. The baywide seagrass restoration goal of 40,000 acres was adopted in 2020. Maintaining adequate water quality at adopted FDEP chlorophyll-a threshold levels in each major bay segment on an annual-average basis is the primary metric for assessing progress toward the seagrass restoration goal. A secondary goal — maintaining hydrologically-normalized total nitrogen loads to each major bay segment — was adopted with the 2009 RA Addendum and later codified as the numeric nutrient criteria for the Tampa Bay estuarine nutrient regions (62-302.532(1), F.A.C.). A compliance assessment framework was established and has been used for all subsequent RA updates (2009 RA Addendum, Section VIII).

title: Overview
section: 2.b. Averaging period:
text:
2.b. Averaging period:
2027 RA Update: No change. The TBEP uses annual-average bay-segment uncorrected chlorophyll-a levels for tracking attainment, as approved by FDEP under the original 2002 RA submittal and adopted in 2012 as NNC. Assessment methods are documented in the tbeptools introduction; source code is at tbep-tech/wq-dash.



Figure 2. Annual-average chlorophyll-a (µg·L⁻¹) for each of the seven FDEP estuarine nutrient regions, 1975–2025. The dotted line in each panel is the FDEP large-exceedance (“+2 se”) threshold.



Figure 2 source: R/figs.R → section annual chl means all segments · Functions: show_rathrplot(), raanlz_avedat() in R/funcs.R · Data: data/chldat.RData

title: Overview
section: 2.c. How will goals result in restoration of impaired designated uses:
text:
2.c. How will goals result in restoration of impaired designated uses:
2027 RA Update: No change. Maintaining chlorophyll-a concentrations at target levels is expected to maintain water clarity adequate to support seagrass at or above 40,000 acres throughout Tampa Bay, ensuring that external nutrient loads do not result in an imbalance in the flora or fauna of Tampa Bay.

title: Overview
section: 2.d. Determining whether additional corrective actions are needed:
text:
2.d. Determining whether additional corrective actions are needed:
2027 RA Update: No changes to the TBEP’s annual management Decision Matrix process, the Tampa Bay NMC nutrient management strategy, or the allocation compliance assessment framework. Results of the bay-segment-specific compliance assessment over the 2022–2026 RA period are described in Figure 11 and Tables 2–6. For the 2022–2026 RA period, no annual exceedances of the chlorophyll-a thresholds nor of hydrologically-normalized total nitrogen loads were observed, and the TN and TP numeric nutrient criteria (Figure 9) were not exceeded.



Figures 3 & 4. Biennial seagrass coverage (× 1,000 acres) by bay segment from the SWFWMD Suncoast seagrass mapping series; 2022–2026 saw increases in all segments except Old Tampa Bay.



Figures 3 & 4 source: R/figs.R → section seagrass coverage by bay segment · Data: SWFWMD Suncoast seagrass series × seagrass segments

title: Overview
section: 3.a. Participating Entities:
text:
3.a. Participating Entities:
2027 RA Update: The Tampa Bay Estuary Program Policy Board includes the City of Tampa, City of Clearwater, City of St. Petersburg, City of Largo, Manatee County, Hillsborough County, Pinellas County, Pasco County, FDEP, the Southwest Florida Water Management District, and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (Ex-officio). The Tampa Bay Nitrogen Management Consortium includes over 45 participating public and private partners — spanning counties and municipalities, state and federal agencies, port and utility interests, and phosphate, agricultural, and industrial partners.

title: Overview
section: 3.b. Existing and proposed management activities:
text:
3.b. Existing and proposed management activities:
2027 RA Update: Consortium participants document completed and planned TN load-reduction projects in the online Tampa Bay Action Plan Database (https://apdb.tbep.org). Corrective-action and restoration projects implemented over 2022–2026 are summarized in the Summary chapter (Section 5).

title: Overview
section: 3.c. Geographic scope of any proposed management activity:
text:
3.c. Geographic scope of any proposed management activity:
2027 RA Update: No change. The NMC Action Plan projects are located throughout the Tampa Bay watershed.

title: Overview
section: 3.d. Estimated Pollutant Load Reduction Anticipated from each activity:
text:
3.d. Estimated Pollutant Load Reduction Anticipated from each activity:
2027 RA Update: Based on projects implemented over 2022–2026, cumulatively an additional 33.1 tons/yr of TN has been precluded from entering Tampa Bay (Table 7). Approximately 106.8 tons/yr of TN is estimated to be precluded after 2026 (Tables 8 & 9).

title: Overview
section: 3.e. Written agreements committing partners to actions:
text:
3.e. Written agreements committing partners to actions:
2027 RA Update: The Tampa Bay Nitrogen Management Consortium gave consensus approval (with no objections) at their 2027 meeting to submit this document to FDEP as the 2027 RA Update for Tampa Bay. Participation status, meeting notes, presentations, and decision memos are at https://tbep.org/our-work/boards-committees/nitrogen-management-consortium/.

title: Overview
section: 3.f. How will future growth and new sources be addressed:
text:
3.f. How will future growth and new sources be addressed:
2027 RA Update: Consistent with prior RA approvals and the 2009 RA Addendum, allocations to all TN loading sources are formalized and cumulatively capped at the federally-recognized TMDL for each bay segment. Reviews of interim, new, and transferred sources led to formal NMC concurrence of allocations assigned to each entity for the 2027–2031 RA implementation period (Tables 10–14), remaining within the TMDL limits.

title: Overview
section: 3.g. Confirmed sources of funding:
text:
3.g. Confirmed sources of funding:
2027 RA Update: No change. Consortium participants abide by recommended funding levels for the NMC’s process to deliver 5-year RA updates. Participants have planned investments of $137,428,003 to continue and implement projects listed in Tables 8 and 9.

title: Overview
section: 3.h. Implementation schedule:
text:
3.h. Implementation schedule:
2027 RA Update: No change. Consortium participants continue to develop future load-reduction projects and document them in the online Tampa Bay Action Plan Database (https://apdb.tbep.org). Table 8 lists ongoing projects; Table 9 lists projects planned to be initiated/completed after 2026.

title: Overview
section: 3.i. Enforcement programs, if the management strategy is not voluntary:
text:
3.i. Enforcement programs, if the management strategy is not voluntary:
2027 RA Update: No change. Participation in the Consortium remains voluntary, and NMC partners continue to encourage non-participating point and nonpoint sources to join. The allocation compliance assessment process (Section 2.a) continues during the 2027–2031 RA implementation period; an assessment of the 2022–2026 period is in Appendices 1–5. FDEP and other regulatory agencies continue to ensure permitted facilities meet all permit requirements through existing regulatory and enforcement programs.

title: Monitoring, Corrective Actions & Summary
text: 4. Procedures for Monitoring and Reporting Results

title: Monitoring, Corrective Actions & Summary
section: 4.a. A description of the water quality monitoring program to be implemented
text:
4.a. A description of the water quality monitoring program to be implemented
2027 RA Update: No change. Existing monitoring includes monthly ambient collections by the Environmental Protection Commission of Hillsborough County, Manatee County, and Pinellas County. Samples from over 100 stations baywide are collected and analyzed monthly. These regional programs are considered among the top in the nation. Additional research investments to understand Old Tampa Bay’s Pyrodinium bahamense bloom dynamics and internal nutrient fluxes have been made or are underway through Tampa Bay Environmental Restoration Fund (TBERF) grants.

title: Monitoring, Corrective Actions & Summary
section: 4.b. Quality Assurance/Quality Control elements of monitoring
text:
4.b. Quality Assurance/Quality Control elements of monitoring
2027 RA Update: No change. All county monitoring programs and laboratories have State-approved Quality Assurance Plans and comply with FDEP’s QA rule (Chapter 62-160), including FDEP-approved SOPs. All participating county laboratories are NELAC certified. Quarterly round-robin inter-laboratory comparisons are conducted by the Southwest Florida Regional Ambient Monitoring Program (SWFL RAMP).

title: Monitoring, Corrective Actions & Summary
section: 4.c. Procedures for entering all appropriate data into WIN/STORET:
text:
4.c. Procedures for entering all appropriate data into WIN/STORET:
2027 RA Update: No change. County programs comply with the latest WIN data-upload procedures developed by FDEP. Through the SWFL RAMP, all Tampa Bay water quality monitoring data providers upload data to WIN.

title: Monitoring, Corrective Actions & Summary
section: 4.d. Responsible monitoring and reporting entity:
text:
4.d. Responsible monitoring and reporting entity:
2027 RA Update: No change. The three entities identified in Section 4.a continue to collect water quality data. TBEP staff and the NMC’s technical support contractor assimilate and summarize the data annually to provide compliance assessment reports to FDEP. Reports for the 2022–2026 RA period are at https://tbep.org/our-work/boards-committees/nitrogen-management-consortium/.

title: Monitoring, Corrective Actions & Summary
section: 4.e. Frequency and reporting format for reporting monitoring results:
text:
4.e. Frequency and reporting format for reporting monitoring results:
2027 RA Update: No change. As part of this update, the TBEP and TBNMC funded development of estimated TN, TP, TSS, and BOD loads for the watershed over the 2022–2026 RA period (https://tbep.org/tampa-bay-nitrogen-loads/). The Consortium also updated a Screening Level Tool for Estimating Annual Hydrologic Loadings to Tampa Bay to assess annual compliance of hydrologically-adjusted allocations; these adjustment factors are reported annually within the NMC compliance assessment reports submitted to FDEP and EPA.

title: Monitoring, Corrective Actions & Summary
section: 4.f. Frequency and format for reporting on the implementation of all proposed management activities:
text:
4.f. Frequency and format for reporting on the implementation of all proposed management activities:
2027 RA Update: No change. Formal reporting of results and action-plan projects continues every 5 years. Annual assessment of bay water quality conditions continues during the 2027–2031 RA Implementation Period.

title: Monitoring, Corrective Actions & Summary
section: 4.g. Methods for evaluating progress towards goals:
text:
4.g. Methods for evaluating progress towards goals:
2027 RA Update: No change. Formal reporting of chlorophyll-a threshold compliance continues annually and integrates new seagrass acreage estimates or trends. If exceedances occur in two consecutive years in any bay segment, additional assessment steps are required. Additionally, the TBNMC re-assessed the assimilative capacity of the Old Tampa Bay segment over the 2022–2026 RA implementation period; revisions to bay-segment load targets, entity allocations, and numeric nutrient criteria were not recommended by the NMC, with FDEP concurring on Mar. 31, 2026 that additional projects and research be pursued in Old Tampa Bay to maintain its reasonable assurance determination.
